title: Early-life antibiotics attenuate regulatory T cell generation and increase the severity of murine house dust mite-induced asthma.
ehr_evidence: C57BL/6J nursing mothers with 3-week-old female pups were purchased from the Jackson Laboratory (Bar Harbor, ME, USA); mice were exposed to three short courses of ABX following weaning and experimental asthma was thereafter induced, with BAL fluid, serum, lung tissue, hilar lymph nodes, and fecal microbiome characterized.
summary: In a murine HDM-induced asthma model, early-life pulsed antibiotic exposure worsened airway inflammation and airway hyper-reactivity and reduced hilar lymph node Tregs, a reduction correlating with decreased fecal microbiome diversity.
key_findings: HDM+ABX Mix animals exhibited threefold higher BAL leukocytosis than HDM alone (29.0 × 10^5 vs. 9.0 × 10^5 cells, p < 0.01)
HDM+ABX Mix animals had twofold higher relative eosinophilia (43% vs. 20%, p < 0.01) and over fivefold higher total eosinophil numbers (14.0 × 10^5 vs. 2.4 × 10^5 eosinophils, p < 0.01)
Serum HDM-specific IgE was significantly higher in HDM+ABX Mix animals (0.95 vs. 0.50 mean AUC, p < 0.05)
HDM+ABX Mix mice had more severe lung histopathology (2.5 vs. 1.5 median score, p < 0.01) with no significant difference in mucus scores
Airway hyper-reactivity (Rrs) was significantly higher in HDM+ABX Mix animals (5.1 vs. 3.8 mean AUC, p < 0.05)
Simpson diversity index was a third higher for HDM vs HDM+ABX Mix (0.954 vs. 0.747, p < 0.01)
HDM+Antibiotic Mix mice had significantly lower proportions of Foxp3+ Tregs as percent of CD4+ T cells (8.9% vs. 11.1%, p < 0.05)
Microbiome diversity positively correlated with Treg proportion (Spearman's r = 0.7109, p < 0.01)
captured_features: Lung histopathology inflammation and mucus scores
Airway hyper-reactivity (total respiratory system resistance, Rrs)
Fecal microbiome diversity (16S rRNA sequencing, Simpson diversity index, LEfSe)
Hilar lymph node Foxp3+ CD4+ regulatory T cell proportions
study_design: Experimental murine model (antibiotic exposure followed by house dust mite-induced allergic airway disease)
population: C57BL/6J mice (female pups weaned at 3 weeks), house dust mite-induced asthma model
exposure_domain: Early-life antibiotic exposure (ampicillin, metronidazole, neomycin, vancomycin)
limitations: The antibiotic cocktail used is unlikely to be utilized clinically
The study does not conclusively establish that immunologic changes are exclusively derived from microbiome disruption, as some antibiotics have direct immunomodulatory properties
Small sample sizes limited some analyses
Results should be applied with caution to other diseases
